caption: We finally worked out which account to pay off first instead of just guessing. Avalanche or snowball — which camp are you in?

slides.body: Bought before the last two rate hikes. Feels tighter than it did on paper.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Family of three, plus the toddler's specific yoghurt demands
slides.body: He eats three different brands of the same yoghurt depending on his mood.

slides.title: Car instalments
slides.body: Shift start times an hour apart. Neither of us can share the one car.

slides.title: Credit card & store accounts
slides.includes: R21 000 combined, 22% and 26% interest, both opened before the wedding
slides.body: We're paying off two accounts neither of us fully remembers filling.

slides.title: Creche
slides.includes: Full day, five days a week
slides.body: Almost a third of what the car instalments cost, and non-negotiable either way.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Medical aid, petrol & insurance, phone & fibre, funeral policies, stokvel, black tax, savings
slides.body: Eighteen thousand five hundred rand of things we'd only ever tracked separately before this.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R48 000 between us. R2 600 of that is the card and the store accounts — we finally ran the avalanche vs snowball numbers instead of guessing which to pay off first.

slides.title: We stopped guessing which account to attack first
slides.body:
We added both accounts to Beyond Horizon's debt tracker and compared the interest cost of avalanche vs snowball.

Snowball wins on momentum. Avalanche saved us the most in interest, so that's the one we picked.

No bank login needed.
